summary: Eco-Tactile maps NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band radar brightness into 3-tier haptic vibrations and ArcGIS StoryMaps, letting anyone see and physically feel surface changes in Lake Tuz, Amazon & Greenland.
details:
Eco-Tactile: NISAR Earth Pulse

What It Does & How It Works Eco-Tactile is a two-part multisensory learning ecosystem that transforms complex NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data into accessible visual stories and physical touch experiences.

  1. Interactive Visual Exploration (ArcGIS StoryMap): Using cloud-penetrating 24 cm wavelength NISAR radar datasets from June and September 2026, we created an interactive Map Tour and before-and-after swipe comparison maps across three critical global regions: Lake Tuz (Türkiye), the Amazon Rainforest (Brazil), and Greenland. Users explore how surface roughness changes—such as water receding into salt crusts, forest canopy clearing, or glacial ice fracturing—alter radar backscatter. To reinforce learning, the StoryMap concludes with an interactive 10-question assessment quiz and a Wordwall activity.
    • 0–85 (Smooth Water / Low Backscatter): No vibration (0 ms)
    • 86–170 (Moist Transition / Medium Roughness): Medium vibration (120 ms)
    • 171–255 (Hard Salt Crust, Dense Canopy, or Fractured Ice): Strong vibration (250 ms)

Benefits & Intended Impact Traditional satellite imagery relies exclusively on sight, making raw radar data abstract for students and inaccessible to kinesthetic learners or visually impaired individuals. Eco-Tactile democratizes Earth observation by turning passive data viewing into active, hands-on exploration. It fosters inclusive Earth literacy in classrooms and empowers anyone to intuitively understand planetary surface changes through both sight and touch.

Tools, Technologies & Data Used

  • Satellite Data: NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band radar datasets retrieved via the Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF) Data Vertex.
  • GIS & Storytelling: Esri ArcGIS StoryMaps (Map Tour, Swipe Comparison Maps) and Wordwall for interactive evaluation.
  • Web & Haptic Development: Built using Bolt.new with React, TypeScript, HTML5 Canvas pixel-luminance sampling, and the Web Vibration API.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered Our core innovation lies in bridging the gap between orbital radar physics and human tactile perception using everyday smartphones—requiring zero specialized hardware. During development, our team prioritized scientific integrity and transparency. While radar backscatter brightness accurately confirms changes in surface structure and roughness, we explicitly highlight in our platform that seasonal moisture, precipitation, or dew can also affect radar signals. Therefore, we educate users that remote sensing observations should be paired with local meteorological and field data before drawing permanent cause-and-effect conclusions. As a future enhancement, we plan to integrate Text-to-Speech (TTS) audio descriptions to provide full multisensory accessibility.
